newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-FROST TAKES THREE-STROKE LEAD IN S.A. PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FROST TAKES THREE-STROKE LEAD IN S.A. PGA.

text.p: South Africa's David Frost fired a third round 66 on Saturday to take the lead in the South African PGA Championship, but saved his fiercest shot for tournament organisers.

"I was angry at the tee times we were given because storms were forecast and if you start late in Johannesburg at this time of year you know you'll have trouble," said Frost after moving to 18-under-par, for a three-stroke lead.

Frost, 37, leads from overnight leader and fellow South African Retief Goosen who bogeyed the last hole for a two-under-par 70, and Japan's Katsuyoshi Tomori who also made five at 18 on his way to 67.
Lightning forced the players off for an hour in the afternoon and and as a result Frost finished his round in near darkness.
"I three putted the 14th hole and took the wrong club off the tee at 15...it was because I was rushing to get the round finished," said Frost.
"I didn't want to have to come back at six a.m. to play a hole and then wait four hours to start the last round."
Tomori and Goosen are a shot ahead of Italy's Massimo Scarpa and South African Nico van Rensburg, while Nick Price of Zimbabwe and first round leader Thomas Gogele of Germany are at 13-under-par.
